name: Treaty with the Blackfeet, 1855 (Lame Bull Treaty)
nations: Blackfoot Confederacy: Amskapi Piikani (Blackfeet / Piegan), Kainai (Blood), Siksika (Blackfoot)
promises: Article 4 recognized a large tract north of the Missouri, from the Rocky Mountains east to the mouth of Milk River, as the territory of the Blackfoot Nation.
Article 3 set aside a common hunting ground south of the Missouri for the Blackfoot and neighboring nations for ninety-nine years.
Article 7 bound the United States to protect the Indians against depredations and unlawful acts by white men living in or passing through their country.
Articles 9 and 10: $20,000 a year in goods and provisions for ten years, and up to $15,000 a year for ten years for farming, trades and schooling.

breaches.what: The Act of April 15, 1874 and the Executive Order of August 19, 1874 took 15,289,344 acres (Royce areas 399 and 574) of the land the Blackfeet and Gros Ventre held under the 1855 treaty. The Court of Claims found that after offsets they were deprived of 12,261,749.76 acres for which they received no compensation, valued when taken at $6,130,874.88.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Act of April 15, 1874, 18 Stat. 28, and Executive Order of August 19, 1874, as found by the Court of Claims in The Blackfeet et al. v. United States, 81 Ct. Cl. 101 (1935), recounted by the Indian Claims Commission (1952)

source.title: Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes v. United States, Docket No. 279, Opinion of the Commission, December 17, 1952
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

breaches.what: For the lands ceded under the Agreement of May 1, 1888 (25 Stat. 113), the Indian Claims Commission found that an agreed consideration of $4,300,000 for lands worth $11,975,324.80 was unconscionable on its face, and held the Blackfeet Nation entitled to recover $11,125,606.40, subject to the consideration paid and offsets.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes v. United States, Docket 279-A, opinion of March 31, 1967 (18 Ind. Cl. Comm. 241)

source.title: Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes v. United States, Docket No. 279-A, Opinion of the Commission, March 31, 1967
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Libraries, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

landTaken: 12,261,749.76 acres taken without compensation under the 1874 Act and order, as found by the Court of Claims (1935); a further cession under the 1888 Agreement, valued at $11,975,324.80 (ICC, 1967).
compensation: The Court of Claims (1935) valued the 1874 taking at $6,130,874.88; the net amount recovered was not located. For the 1888 cession the ICC fixed liability at $11,125,606.40 to the Blackfeet before consideration and offsets (1967); final judgments for the Blackfeet and Gros Ventre followed in 1968 but were not read.
today: Not researched past the 1968 judgments. The Blackfeet Reservation today lies within the 1855 treaty area.

nationVoice.summary: The Nation says the original 1855 Blackfeet Indian Reservation took in most of the northern half of Montana, while the present reservation in northwest Montana, bordered by Glacier National Park and Canada, spans 1.5 million acres.

plain.promised: A large territory north of the Missouri recognized as the Blackfoot Nation's, a shared hunting ground for ninety-nine years, protection from white men, and yearly goods and schooling for ten years.
plain.happened: An 1874 Act and executive order took 15,289,344 acres; the Court of Claims found in 1935 that no compensation was paid for 12,261,749.76 acres. The Indian Claims Commission found the 1888 cession price unconscionable in 1967.
plain.today: The Court of Claims valued the 1874 taking at $6,130,874.88; the net amount recovered has not been traced. Final judgments for the 1888 cession followed in 1968 but have not been read.

openQuestions: The 1935 Court of Claims opinion (81 Ct. Cl. 101) was not opened directly; its findings are taken from the Indian Claims Commission's 1952 account.

Audit 2026-11-08: the sentence that the Commission "found" the 1874 Act reduced the tribes' interest by 4,318,919 acres without consent was removed from the 1967 breach. In the opinion (pointer 2749) that figure is in an argument the Commission quotes ("it is believed that the Court should not have charged..."), not in a finding.

The 1910 Act taking timber, hunting and fishing rights reserved in the 1896 agreement for the Glacier National Park area was denied by the Court of Claims and was not researched further; Blackfeet treaty rights in the park remain disputed.
The Blackfeet Nation's own website blocked automated access; no nation account was recorded. The Gros Ventre (Fort Belknap Indian Community) account was not sought.
Royce records that an 1868 treaty with the Blackfeet was never ratified and that an Executive Order of July 5, 1873 set apart a joint reserve partly from the 1855 territory.
